QF.id: AIFM CIII Governance and Due Diligence_27

question.text: As per SEBI rules, if the AIF is established as a TRUST, then losses/damages/expenses incurred by the Manager or its officers in relation to resolution of investor claims/disputes:

answer.text: Shall be met out of the trust property
Shall NOT be met out of the trust property
Shall be passed on to distributors

explanation.text: The Logic: Per Chapter 11.3.7 (end): if the AIF has been established as a trust, no loss/damage/expense incurred by the Manager or its officers, including those in relation to resolution of investor claims/disputes, shall be met out of the trust property. This protects the corpus. The Trap: 'Met out of trust property' is the common trap — it's opposite of the rule. SEBI refund and distributor-pass-through options are absurd. Cross-Exam Context: Same corpus-protection rule in XIX-C/D. Important in SEBI on-site inspections. Manager's Pro-Tip: Buy a robust Manager E&O and D&O policy sized to cover at least 2 years of fund expenses + legal provisions — the corpus cannot bail out the manager under this rule, and one major grievance defence cost can otherwise wipe out fee income for the year.
